newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up on exporter activity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up on exporter activity.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed early fall to close higher against its American counterpart on Tuesday amid late U.S. dollar sales from exporters, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$27.545, off a T$27.609 low, against Monday's T$27.573 close. Turnover through dealers was a heavy US$349 million.
The Taiwan dollar opened fairly lower to react to the strength of the U.S. dollar overseas.
"But seeing the Taiwan dollar unable to fall further, exporters emerged to sell U.S. dollars actively, causing the reversal," said one dealer.
Another dealer said the local unit unable to fall further to break recent support of T$27.62 because the month-end U.S. dollar demand has neared its end.
"The Taiwan dollar's rise against early fall was also because of the (downward correction) of the U.S. dollar in afternoon trade overseas," the dealer said.
Dealers described the exporters' U.S. dollar sales as cut-loss or disappointed selling.
For Wednesday, a T$27.52-27.57 range was seen.
